The '''2025–26 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] for the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by coach [[Hubert Davis]] in his fifth and final season as UNC's head coach, and was assisted by [[Jeff Lebo]], [[Sean May]], and Brad Frederick. The Tar Heels played their home games at the [[Dean Smith Center]] in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC).

The Tar Heels began the season ranked twenty-fifth in the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|AP poll]] and won their first five games in a row. The highlight of the winning streak was a 87–74 victory over nineteenth-ranked [[2025–26 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. The team then traveled to [[Fort Myers, Florida]] to participate in the [[Fort Myers Tip-Off]]. They extended their winning streak to six games with a defeat of [[2025–26 St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball team|St. Bonaventure]], but it ended there with a loss to eleventh-ranked [[2025–26 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. The Tar Heels rose to sixteenth in the AP poll over the streak. The team defeated [[Kentucky–North Carolina basketball rivalry|rivals]], eighteenth-ranked [[2025–26 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] after the loss in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]]. They went on to win their remaining five non-conference games to finish non-conference play with a record of 12–1 and ranked twelfth. They only faced one further Power-4 opponent over this run, [[2025–26 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the [[CBS Sports Classic]]. The Tar Heels began conference play on a 2–3 run which saw them fall to twenty-second in the AP poll. They defeated [[2025–26 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] to start ACC play and [[North Carolina–Wake Forest rivalry|rivals]] [[2025–26 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] over the stretch but lost road games against [[2025–26 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]], [[2025–26 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]], and [[2025–26 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]]. The team turned it around and went 5–0 in their next five games. They defeated fourteenth-ranked [[2025–26 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] on the road and fourth-ranked [[Duke–North Carolina rivalry|rivals]] [[2025–26 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] to rise to eleventh in the rankings. They went 3–2 over their next five games, losing at [[2025–26 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] and at [[North Carolina–NC State rivalry|rivals]] [[2025–26 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]]. They defeated twenty-fourth ranked [[2025–26 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] by three points during this stretch. They finished the season by defeating [[2025–26 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] and [[2025–26 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] but losing to top-ranked Duke on the final day of the regular season.

The Tar Heels finished the season 24–9 overall and 12–6 in [[2025–26 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for fourth place. As the fourth seed in the [[2026 ACC men's basketball tournament|2026 ACC tournament]], they earned a double-bye into the Quarterfinals where they were defeated Clemson by a point. The team earned an at-large bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were the six-seed in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#South regional – Houston, Texas|South region]]. They were upset by eleven-seed [[2025–26 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]] in [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]] in the First Round after being up by as many as nineteen points in the second half. After the loss, head coach [[Hubert Davis]] was fired.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48300016/source-hubert-davis-fired-north-carolina-hoops-coach|title=Hubert Davis fired as North Carolina men's basketball coach|work=[[ESPN]]|author1=Pete Thamel|author2=Jeff Borzello|date=March 24, 2026|access-date=May 4, 2026}}</ref>

==Previous season==
{{main|2024–25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team}}
The Tar Heels finished the 2024–25 season with a 23–14 overall record, with a 13–7 mark in the ACC, tying for 4th in the league. The team faced many ups and downs, starting with a tough non-conference schedule facing teams like [[2024–25 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]], [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]], [[2024–25 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]], [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], and [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. The Heels showed flashes when rallying from a 21‑point second‑half deficit to defeat Dayton in the Maui Invitational,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://goheels.com/news/2024/11/26/mens-basketball-mbb-maui-recap-vs-dayton|title=Trimble & Davis Lead Big Comeback Win Over Dayton, 92-90|first=Matt|last=Bowers|website=goheels.com|publisher=Go Heels|date=November 26, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2025}}</ref> and overcame a 16-point hole vs. UCLA in the CBS Sports Classic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://goheels.com/news/2024/12/21/mens-basketball-mbb-recap-vs-ucla|title=Defense, Jackson Lead Big Comeback Win Over UCLA, 76-74|first=Matt|last=Bowers|website=goheels.com|publisher=Go Heels|date=December 21, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2025}}</ref>

As the No. 5 seed in the ACC Tournament, they defeated [[2024-25 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] in the second round, [[2024-25 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] in the quarterfinals, and fell short in a comeback bid against [[2024-25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the semifinals. UNC earned an at-large bid to the NCAA Tournament as an 11 seed in the South Region, starting their tournament in Dayton at the First Four. They routed [[2024-25 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]] 95–68 to advance to the round of 64, but their run ended there with a 71–64 loss to [[2024-25 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]].

==Offseason==
The Tar Heels lost virtually their entire core, including all five starters from the 2024–25 season. Among the most notable departures were veteran guard RJ Davis and forward Jae'Lyn Withers, both of whom graduated. Numerous players entered the transfer portal, including Elliot Cadeau, Ian Jackson, Jalen Washington, and Ven-Allen Lubin. Freshman Drake Powell decided to enter the 2025 NBA Draft. The only main rotation player that announced he would be returning was guard Seth Trimble.

UNC aggressively rebuilt its roster through the transfer portal, international signings, and high school recruits. The additions were led by several transfers, including 7-footer Henri Veesaar from Arizona, forward Jarin Stevenson from Alabama, and guard Kyan Evans from Colorado State. They also brought in wing shooter Jonathan Powell from West Virginia, and international guard Luka Bogavac from Montenegro. They also added incoming freshmen, most notably five-star forward Caleb Wilson, along with guards Derek Dixon and Isiah Denis.
